confidence_notes: I used 4 of the 6 allowed web searches: 1 for the RBA exchange rate and 3 for food and drink prices. The FX figure is the RBA 4:00 pm AUD/USD rate of 0.6720 for 18 November 2026. The search result named the RBA Exchange Rates Overview page as its source. The food and drink anchors come from cost-of-living and guide sites (MyLifeElsewhere, Expat Exchange, Exiap, Nomad.watch, CityCost, Traveltables) and some undated menu listings for bars near Pub Street. These sources do not give clear dates, so they may not reflect July 2026 prices exactly. The restaurant meal and coffee anchors are the most reliable. Three-course meals for two are listed at about $21-24, with ranges of $15-30. Inexpensive meals are about $2.50-5. Cappuccinos are about $1.50-2.50. Draft beer varies widely. Happy-hour draft can cost $0.50-1, while restaurant listings show local beer at about $1-2, so I used a sit-down restaurant price. The cocktail and wine anchors are less certain. Venue listings show cocktails from $3.50 to about $7 and house wine at about $4-5 a glass. I used a midpoint for each and did not rely only on the usual price ratio to beer. As instructed, I did not search for accommodation prices. Those 4 anchors are general-knowledge estimates and are the least certain. They assume July, which is the green or low season, when room rates in Siem Reap are usually lower than in the December-February peak. Tourism in the city recovered only partly after the pandemic.
comparable_city_reasoning: I checked Siem Reap against other tourist hubs in mainland Southeast Asia, such as Phnom Penh, Luang Prabang and Chiang Mai. Food and drink in Siem Reap are a little cheaper than in Phnom Penh. Hostel and guesthouse rates are among the lowest in the region because there is a lot of budget accommodation and demand drops in the low season.
